newsitem.title: USA: Cisco makes acquisitions, takes charges.
newsitem.headline: Cisco makes acquisitions, takes charges.

text.p: SAN JOSE, Calif., June 24 (REUTER) - Cisco Systems Inc said Tuesday it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire privately held Ardent Communications Corp for $156 million of Cisco common stock.
In connection with the deal, the company said it expects a one-time charge against after-tax earnings of $0.23 per share in the fourth fiscal quarter of 1997.
In a separate announcement, the company also said it was in a pact to buy Global Internet Software Group, a wholly owned subsidiary of Global Internet.Com Inc, for about $40.25 million in cash.
The company said it expects the Global Internet deal to result in a one-time charge against after-tax earnings of between $0.02 and $0.03 per share in the fourth fiscal quarter of 1997.

Cisco said it is also taking an undisclosed minority equity interest in parent company Global Internet.Com, which builds, manages and secures corporate networks with a focus on medium-size business. Global Internet Software specializes in security solutions for Microsoft Windows NT Networks.
The company said it expects both deals to close in late July, subject to various closing conditions.

San Jose-based Ardent, in which Cisco said it previously held a minority stake along with Sequoia Capital, designs, manufacturers and distributes advanced access products for integrating voice, video and data on public or private Frame Relay or ATM networks.
